sub_units.name: Creating a Database
sub_units.content: The CREATE DATABASE statement is used to create a new SQL database. It is the first step in setting up a data storage environment. Once created, you can start defining tables and relationships within it.

sub_units.name: Creating Tables
sub_units.content: The CREATE TABLE statement is used to create a new table in a database. You must specify the table name and define its columns, including their data types and any initial constraints.

sub_units.name: Modifying Tables (ALTER TABLE)
sub_units.content: The ALTER TABLE statement is used to add, delete, or modify columns in an existing table. It is also used to add and drop various constraints on an existing table without deleting the entire table.

sub_units.name: Deleting Tables (DROP, TRUNCATE)
sub_units.content: DROP TABLE is used to remove a table definition and all data, indexes, triggers, constraints, and permission specifications for that table. TRUNCATE TABLE removes all rows from a table, but the table structure and its columns, constraints, indexes, and so on remain.

sub_units.name: Constraints
sub_units.content: Constraints are used to specify rules for the data in a table. Common constraints include PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, DEFAULT, and Auto Increment. They ensure data accuracy and reliability.

sub_units.name: Relationships (1-1, 1-M, M-M)
sub_units.content: Database relationships define how tables are linked together. The three main types are One-to-One (1-1), One-to-Many (1-M), and Many-to-Many (M-M). Relationships are typically implemented using Foreign Keys.

sub_units.name: Introduction to ER Diagrams
sub_units.content: An Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagram is a visual representation of the database structure. It shows entities (tables), attributes (columns), and relationships between them, helping in the design phase of a database.

sub_units.name: Normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF
sub_units.content: Normalization is the process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity. It involves dividing large tables into smaller ones and defining relationships between them (1NF, 2NF, 3NF).
